# Validation record

The committed reports were generated locally on 2026-09-07 with Windows 11,
Python 3.13.5, MinGW g++ 8.1.0 (-O3, C++17), and MATLAB R2025a.
Exact OS/processor and language-version fields are in results/*.json.
The Linux CI workflow is supplied but has not been run remotely as part of
this local validation.

## Independent checks

- 196 small-code/cutoff cases use a direct exhaustive oracle. The oracle
  encodes with $G_{ij}=\mathbf1\{(i\mathbin{\&}j)=j\}$ and checks original
  constraints before projection. It does not invoke production GF(2)
  preprocessing, Count/Gen, affine counting, or WEF recursion.
- Cases include N=1,2,4,8,16; static/dynamic/redundant/noncanonical checks;
  no, partial, or complete projection; shortening; D=0 and full small spectra.
- Each case runs under auto, enumerate, and dp. Both Python and C++ are
  compared independently with the oracle.
- An additional unconstrained N=128, D=24 case checks every coefficient
  against the exact binomial coefficient. This exercises counts beyond 2^53
  and 2^64.
- MATLAB runs the same 197 cases under all three policies:
  **591 comparisons**. Its expected vectors are saved in tests/oracle_vectors.json
  and regenerated by tools/make_test_vectors.py.
- Direct PAC convolution verifies the tap direction and frozen-source checks.
  Additional tests cover invalid input and explicit work-limit failure.

## Fixed profiles

All 24 combinations of N∈{64,128,256}, kind∈{Polar,PAC}, and
mode∈{none,puncture,shorten,mixed} agree across Python, C++, and MATLAB
at D=8, including all four dimension fields.

For the unmodified mother codes:

| N,K | Polar nonzero terms through 8 | PAC nonzero terms through 8 |
|---|---|---|
| 64,32 | 664 X^8 | 472 X^8 |
| 128,64 | 432 X^8 | 320 X^8 |
| 256,128 | 96 X^8 | 96 X^8 |

Add 1 for the zero codeword in each row. These results refer to the exact
committed GA and tap conventions, not every construction sharing the same
N,K labels.

## Timing

The Python/C++ report uses one warm-up and seven timed runs per case.
Across the 24 cases, the median algorithm times in this local run were
approximately 3.7–8.3 ms in Python and 0.42–0.84 ms in C++.
MATLAB's profile checks took approximately 51–145 ms per call after the
oracle tests; these are single-run measurements and are not a matched
seven-run benchmark.

These are implementation sanity measurements for D=8, not a general
speedup claim, an SCL baseline comparison, or evidence of scalability for
all cutoffs. Preprocessing plus counting is measured; startup and profile
construction are excluded. C++ binding overhead is recorded separately.

## Reproduction

~~~shell
python tools/build_cpp.py
python -m pytest -q
python tools/make_test_vectors.py
~~~

In MATLAB:

~~~matlab
addpath('tests');
test_matlab;
~~~

Then:

~~~shell
python tools/benchmark.py --repeat 7
~~~

Local packaging checks also built the CMake target, imported the Python wheel
in isolated mode, and ran the (64,32) PAC mixed-pattern example at D=12 in all
three languages. Its saved spectrum is in results/example_pac_64_mixed_D12.json.
The Python/C++ pytest run passed all 50 test items.

The final command reads the MATLAB report, verifies each matching spectrum
and dimension, and saves the Python/C++ timings. The pytest suite intentionally
also supports pure-Python environments; build the native library first to
include C++ comparisons.
